text:
jordan: heads up — we just saw a massive gpu-provisioner stall in eu-west-2 for ~8min. pods queued with `ImagePull`->`ContainerCreating` and then failed scheduling. node-gpu-17 had nvme io wait pegged.

maya: same cluster. I saw local-ssd pool IOPS drop to near 0 while queue depth stayed full. SMART looks clean but reallocated_sector_ct ticked up by 1 on node-gpu-17 this morning :grimacing:

devon: interesting — any chance this is the ephemeral-cleaner compaction + periodic fstrim overlap? In the past concurrent discard across devices caused big queue stalls on some NVMe firmware.

jordan: logs show a pile of discard ioctl -> block layer backpressure. snippet from node-gpu-17 dmesg:
```
[2025-11-09T02:13:42Z] nvme0: io 134217728 completed with status -EIO after 120000ms
[2025-11-09T02:13:42Z] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[2025-11-09T02:13:43Z] blk-mq: queue 0 blocked for more than 120s
```

sre-bot: alert: disk_io_stall on node-gpu-17 (eu-west-2) — 2025-11-09T02:14:00Z — autoscale suppressed for pool-ssd-euwest2

maya: iostat during the window (1s samples) showed kdq==0, await skyrocketed, util ~100% but throughput ~0. Few writes made it through — consistent with firmware-level discard stall.

devon: short mitigation I pushed to canary: add exponential backoff to ephemeral-cleaner discard worker and disable scheduled fstrim during heavy provisioning windows. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/patch/3245

jordan: deployed canary to 3 nodes in pool-ssd-euwest2 — will monitor. also applied a temporary kernel knob to reduce outstanding requests: 
```
echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests
echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/block_dump  # debug only
```

ops-rotation: plan: roll the rest of pool at 02:00 UTC with the backoff patch + disable scheduled fstrim for 24h. if we see no regressions we'll bake into release. tagging @oncall to watch provisioning latency.

maya: noted. after the canary the provisioning latency dropped from 480s -> 45s on those hosts. :thumbsup:

devon: follow-up items:
- add firmware-safe-discard flag to node labels so provisioner can opt-out
- region runbook write-up for eu-west-2 nvme quirks
- schedule a vendor firmware check on nodes with reallocated counts >0

jordan: thanks — i'll add the runbook snippet in #eng-infra/runbooks and schedule vendor contact. saving logs under /var/log/nvme-diagnostics/node-gpu-17-20251109.tar.gz

sre-bot: note: incident closed (mitigated) 2025-11-09T03:20:00Z
